cards.front: What does the Package class actually hold?
cards.back: Version metadata about a package's specification and implementation — not the package's classes
cards.extra: The ClassLoader creates it from information typically stored in the JAR manifest: title, version and vendor strings.

cards.front: How do you get the Package object for a class?
cards.extra: The static method searches the caller's ClassLoader, so it can return null when that loader knows nothing about the package.

cards.front: How many Package objects exist for one package name?
cards.back: One per ClassLoader — all classes from the same package loaded by that loader share it
cards.extra: Two different loaders can each have their own Package object for the same name, which is why package identity in Java is loader-qualified.

cards.front: What syntax must a specification version follow?
cards.back: Non-negative decimal integers separated by dots — "1.2.3.4"
cards.extra: Comparison is numeric per component, most significant first, so 1.10 is greater than 1.9.

cards.back: That this package's specification version is greater than or equal to the desired one
cards.extra: It throws NumberFormatException if either string is not in dotted-numeric form, so it cannot be used with arbitrary vendor versions.

cards.front: How should implementation versions be compared?
cards.back: Only for equality — they have no specified syntax
cards.extra: They are vendor strings. Treating them as ordered numbers is a portability bug.

cards.back: All classes in the package must come from the same code source (same JAR or directory)
cards.extra: It prevents an attacker from adding a class to an existing package and gaining its package-private access. isSealed(URL) tests it against a specific source.

cards.front: How do you annotate a whole package?
cards.back: In package-info.java — Package implements AnnotatedElement, so the annotations are readable at runtime
cards.extra: That is the only place package-level annotations and Javadoc can live; there is no syntax for annotating a package declaration inside a normal class file.
